description: We are 6 high schoolers that love to build things that have real impact over people.
summary: Project Astrophage turns 45 years of NASA observations into a delivery decision for malaria medicine in Eastern Province, Zambia. We test nine climate indicators in all 28 NASA POWER grid cells covering the province, seasons 1981/82 to 2025/26, using Sen’s slope, Mann–Kendall and a Benjamini–Hochberg correction across cells. October is warmer in 27 of the 28 cells and the wettest day is heavier in 13, while total wet-season rainfall shows no significant trend anywhere: the season has changed shape, not size, which is exactly what the fixed calendars behind medicine deliveries cannot see. But a grid cell spans roughly 56 × 67 km, so a trend is not yet a place. That is why Pod K-01, a 3D-printable sensor box, reads air, pulse and SpO2 on site while two small neural networks listen through the microphone for mosquitoes, and why danger-sign questions then set a referral, an order and a road route from the nearest hub. It all runs from pre-built files in the browser, with no server, no API key and no connection, because the clinics that need it have the worst internet. The code, the data scripts and the pod’s CAD files are open.
details:
Project Astrophage is an application that bridges the climate and health data in Eastern Province, Zambia through NASA POWER data, health and environmental sensors, and mosquito sound recognition. It illustrates the process through which a team of health professionals would identify the danger signals, compose a prescription for medicines, and decide on a delivery pathway.

We developed the application using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. For the backend, we utilized Python and PyTorch for data processing and machine learning, OpenStreetMap data for roads, and a Seeed XIAO board with pulse, blood oxygen, temperature, and humidity sensors.

Our project is innovative due to the integration of climate analysis, sensor readings, mosquito recognition, and health response into one application. We designed the application to be available offline and to provide a clear depiction of uncertainties. The application's goal is to provide easy-to-comprehend environmental data and to inspire communities to explore strategies to adapt to the changing conditions.
